key_agent_trends: Agent infrastructure funding accelerates as Daytona reaches unicorn status for specialized cloud sandboxes tailored to short-lived, stateful agent jobs.
Open-source agent tooling matures with TanStack AI 1.0 delivering a stable, provider-agnostic toolkit including sandboxes, subagents and experimental long-running harnesses.
Specialized low-latency decision APIs become production-ready, enabling agents and apps to make high-volume classification and routing choices far more efficiently than general-purpose models.

stories.headline: Daytona raises $60M Series B at $1B valuation for agent cloud infrastructure
stories.what_happened: Daytona Platforms announced a $60 million Series B led by FirstMark Growth at a $1 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $91 million. The company builds specialized cloud infrastructure for AI agents that spin up thousands of short-lived, stateful sandboxes supporting Linux, Windows, macOS and GPU environments. Notable angels include Patrick Collison, Tobi Lütke, Aravind Srinivas, Eric Yuan and Adam D’Angelo.
stories.why_it_matters: It signals strong investor conviction that existing cloud primitives are insufficient for agent workloads, and that specialized, low-latency sandbox infrastructure will be a critical layer as agents move from demos to production-scale execution.

stories.headline: TanStack AI reaches 1.0 with stable agent toolkit and experimental harness
stories.what_happened: TanStack published version 1.0 of its AI stack on October 23, 2026, stabilizing 76 packages. The release formally supports agents, subagents, coding-agent workflows, sandboxes, 23 provider adapters, and an experimental harness for long-running agents that persist across restarts and support mid-turn steering.
stories.why_it_matters: It gives developers a mature, framework- and provider-agnostic open-source alternative for building production agent applications, reducing lock-in and simplifying the embedding of tool-calling and coding agents across web apps and editors.

stories.headline: OpenAI makes Decisions API generally available for fast agent routing and classification
stories.what_happened: On October 22, 2026, OpenAI announced general availability of the Decisions API, powered by GPT-6 Luna. It returns probabilities, choices or scores for bounded questions up to 10x faster than the Responses API, with pricing of $0.10 per million input tokens and no output charge. Requests now support up to 400 questions, native JSON, images and prompt caching.
stories.why_it_matters: It provides a production-ready, low-cost primitive for the high-volume micro-decisions agents and applications make throughout workflows, such as classification, routing and next-action selection, without the latency or cost of full generative calls.
